reply.summary: Wrote docs/designs/017-keybinding-extraction-codecs/01-research.md for ADR-017 (codec families, config-path discovery, bindings/v1 snapshot, read-only `discovery bindings` face). Read set: the ADR plus its cited ADRs 008, 009, 012, 013, 022, 023, 025, the ADR/task directory listings, and 13 additional repo files (crates/discovery, crates/core/src/input.rs, schemas/README.md, schemas/manifests/v1/spec.md, apps/discovery-cli) plus web sources for Steam userdata/controller_config layouts, Proton prefix layout and symlink fragility, Unreal INI/config hierarchy and Enhanced Input persistence, Source cfg grammar, and Unreal text encoding. No prior run artifacts existed in the design directory. Key research outputs: today's scan cannot name the main Steam root (roots are unioned and flattened) so 017-C2 is new plumbing; the closed ADR-012 input vocabulary (48 keyboard glyphs, no modifiers/named keys/axes) cannot spell most real bindings, which collides with 017-C3/L3; 013-B4 is the wrong bound for a codec family id (the spec uses the shared MAX_SLUG_OCTETS); bindings/v1's JSON 'document verbatim' makes it the second JSON format unless schemas/README is amended; 025-L5 forbids source keys in shipped artifacts, which the snapshot's lookup key and SteamID may violate; 013-R2/R3 name ADR-017 as owner and the ADR never mentions them; and reuse of list's scan drags 025-L1's mandatory catalog probe into a face the ADR calls local-by-construction. 15 open questions are handed to the designer.
reply.commitMessage: docs: add 017 research on keybinding extraction codec families
docs: add 017 design proposal for keybinding extraction codec families

findings.location: Config-path resolvers — "`NativeHost`: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when set and absolute, else `$HOME/.config`, with `user` the constant `host`"
findings.problem: Unlike SteamUserdata (`<ctx.root>/userdata/<dir>/<ctx.appid>`) and ProtonPrefix (`…/compatdata/<ctx.appid>/pfx/…`), the NativeHost template carries no appid, so its tree is the host's shared config root for every application. `detect` then "walk[s] each `UserTree` depth-first … collecting `*.ini` files whose path ends `Saved/Config/<one directory>/<name>.ini`" to MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH = 8 from that root, so on a machine with two Unreal titles writing `~/.config/<ProjectName>/Saved/Config/Linux/GameUserSettings.ini`, `discovery bindings steam/<appidA>` locates title B's user config and reports its actions and inputs under title A's lookup key (the located set is truncated to the first 32 in byte order, so which foreign file appears is a directory-ordering accident). That contradicts 017-L3 ("A snapshot states only what a located file states") and falsifies §The first family's "grammar-driven location inside a tree the context owns" — the context owns nothing of `$HOME/.config`. The `native-linux` fixture carries one game, so no test exposes it.
findings.fix: Make the native tree game-scoped or drop it this run: either scope `NativeHost` to `<config>/<one directory>` whose name the record can justify (replacing the sentence "no UE project name is guessed"), or return no `NativeHost` tree until 017-R4 supplies project/appid routing, move the native launcher context to Deferred, and record 017-S1's "native … contexts" as a divergence in the Revision log.

findings.location: GameContext (017-C2) — "pub root: PathBuf,        // the owning root: `userdata/` lives here (A18)"
findings.problem: 017-C2 asks for "every steam root the scan resolved — main root and library roots separately, because `userdata/` lives only under the main root", but this context carries one root: the library's owner ("the root itself, or the root whose `libraryfolders.vdf` named it"). When more than one full install is in play — which A3 states as fact — owner and main root differ, and SteamUserdata is resolved under the wrong root, so a game that does have `userdata/` answers claim-refused or family-confirmed-files-absent. The sentence also states as fact what A18, marked `unverified`, states about the *main* root; and this divergence from the source's wording is not among §Context's declared "Three clauses of the source … implemented differently than worded" nor recorded in the Revision log.
findings.fix: Resolve `userdata/` against every root the scan resolved (the union of existing `<root>/userdata/<dir>/<appid>`, byte order) and delete the "`userdata/` lives here" comment; or keep the single owning root and add a Revision-log entry recording the narrowing of 017-C2, with its unit id in Rollout 8's amended-by hand-off.

findings.location: Config-path resolvers with The codec face and Determinism — "`env` is a lookup closure, mirroring `steam_linux::host_candidates` and `matches::store_path`, so every rule here is unit-tested without touching the process environment"
findings.problem: In production the closure has no supplier: `detect` is pinned by 017-C1 as `fn detect(&self, ctx: &GameContext) -> Option<Detection>`, so the family must call `user_trees(ctx, &|k| std::env::var(k).ok())` itself and read `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`HOME` from the process. 017-L4 says the opposite — "nothing about wall-clock time, environment beyond the context, or registry iteration order can reach an artifact" — and §Determinism restates the law with that clause dropped ("Nothing reads wall-clock time, and nothing about registry iteration order or directory-return order reaches an artifact"), so one GameContext with identical file contents yields different snapshots under different `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. Test strategy #12 cannot see it: it shuffles "the registry and the `UserTree` vector", never the environment. The unverified-A18/`NativeHost` path in finding 2 runs through this same env read.
findings.fix: Carry the resolved host config root in `GameContext` as `Option<PathBuf>`, filled by the CLI from the same env closure `store_path` is given at apps/discovery-cli/src/main.rs:113, and drop the `env` parameter from `user_trees` — this replaces the process-env read rather than adding a knob; or record the narrowing of 017-L4's environment clause in the Revision log and add the env-varied case to #12.

findings.location: Test strategy #16 with Rollout 9 — "the workspace `Cargo.lock` is unchanged" / "any `Cargo.lock` change is a finding"
findings.problem: `crates/codecs` joins the existing `crates/*` glob (Cargo.toml:12), and every current workspace member is recorded in the root lockfile (bindforge-core, bindforge-registry, bindforge-transforms, discovery, discovery-cli), so adding a member necessarily adds a `[[package]] name = "bindforge-codecs"` entry — and `cargo test --workspace --locked` fails when the lockfile is stale. The pin is unsatisfiable as written, and Rollout 9 instructs the reviewer to treat a mandatory change as a defect. §crates/codecs and the Compatibility matrix state it correctly as "no `Cargo.lock` **version** change", so the document contradicts itself.
findings.fix: Restate #16 as "the lockfile's external package set and every resolved version are unchanged; the only delta is the `bindforge-codecs` entry and its path edges", and narrow Rollout 9 to "any change to an external dependency or its version is a finding".

findings.location: Read discipline and budgets — "one extraction opens at most `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` files, so its worst-case read cost is `16 × 32 × MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS` (512 MiB)"
findings.problem: MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME bounds only "`userdata/` directories considered per game", but `user_trees` returns three template families: up to 16 SteamUserdata trees plus one ProtonPrefix plus one NativeHost, each with its own capped located set (§The first family: "capped at `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` per tree"). The aggregate product that ships to `schemas/README.md` is understated by two trees — 512 files stated against 576 possible.
findings.fix: Name `MAX_USER_TREES_PER_GAME = 18` (or `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 2`), bound the resolvers with it, and state the aggregate as `MAX_USER_TREES_PER_GAME × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` (576 MiB).

findings.location: The first family — "Accepted lines: `[Section]` headers, `Key=Value`, `+Key=Value`, `-Key=Value`, and `.Key=Value` as UE's documented line-continuation"
findings.problem: The source A15 cites documents four operators, not three: `+` adds if absent, `-` removes on exact match, `.` "Adds a new property … like `+` except it will potentially add a duplicate line" — not a line-continuation, which is what Test strategy #7 then pins as "`.Key=` continuation joins" — and `!`, which "Removes a property; but you do not have to have an exact match, just the name". A `!Bindings=(…)` line is therefore out-of-grammar and silently skipped, so the snapshot keeps reporting a binding the file removed: the same silent drift the section says it refuses ("drift becomes loud rather than a silently shorter snapshot"), in the opposite direction.
findings.fix: Add `!Key=` to the accepted set as a removal from the working set, or name it `UnparsableEntry` beside the broken-tuple case, and restate `.` per the cited doc as an add that may duplicate; re-word #7 to match.

findings.location: The codec face (017-C1) — "fn extract(&self, claim: &Detection) -> Result<Vec<BindingSnapshot>, ExtractionRefusal>"
findings.problem: 017-C1 words the same method as "`extract(&Detection) -> Result<BindingSnapshot, ExtractionRefusal>`" (singular). The Vec is the right resolution of the ADR's own C1/C3 tension and the section argues for it, but it is a fourth reading that differs from the source's wording, while §Context claims exactly "Three clauses of the source are implemented differently than worded" and the Revision log carries no entry for it — so the run's divergence accounting is incomplete for a ledger ADR.
findings.fix: One Revision-log line — 017-C1's `extract` returns one document per located user tree, not one document — and add that unit id to Rollout 8's amended-by hand-off.

findings.location: The CLI face with Determinism (017-L4) — "More than one record matching (one game in two libraries) is not an error: each is processed and rendered"
findings.problem: The NativeHost tree depends on nothing in the record, so one game installed in two libraries locates the same tree twice and `--json` prints the same snapshot document twice; and since §bindings/v1 restricts `user` to "a SteamID, `steamuser`, `host`", no field distinguishes the two, leaving the law's "across documents, byte order by `user`" with an unordered tie and the artifact stating one fact twice.
findings.fix: In CLI step 4, deduplicate documents by (`user`, `provenance.files`) before sorting and rendering, and state that in §Determinism so the ordering law has no tie.

findings.location: Test strategy #15 — "the boundary sweep skips exactly `schemas/bindings/`"
findings.problem: Contract-tree amendment 4 makes the skip set `SOURCE_KEY_TREES: [&str; 2] = ["catalog", "bindings"]`, so "exactly" contradicts the amendment (and the existing `data/catalog/` skip).
findings.fix: "the boundary sweep skips exactly `data/catalog/`, `schemas/catalog/` and `schemas/bindings/`".

findings.location: Read discipline (never-write) — "every open is `FileOptions::new().read(true)` and nothing else"
findings.problem: `FileOptions` is not a name the crate can write; the type is `std::fs::OpenOptions`.
findings.fix: Name `std::fs::OpenOptions::new().read(true)`.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — Flatpak / Snap Steam row: "The face inherits `host_candidates` roots (A3) unchanged, and every candidate template is relative to the owning root, not `$HOME`"
findings.problem: [new] The premise is false of one of the three shipped resolvers: §Config-path resolvers defines `NativeHost` as `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, else `$HOME/.config`, read from the BindForge process's own environment, so it is root-independent; only `SteamUserdata` and `ProtonPrefix` are root-relative. A Flatpak/Snap Steam install puts a native-launched game's `$HOME` inside the package (`$HOME/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/config/…`, `~/snap/steam/common/.config/…`), which no shipped template reaches, so the row's unqualified `Yes` is overclaimed — such a title answers no-claim. Evidence: crates/discovery/src/steam_linux.rs:112-125 against the proposal's own `NativeHost` rule.
findings.fix: Narrow the row to what the templates cover: root-relative trees Yes, sandboxed launcher's own config home not searched (native-context title answers no-claim), and either derive a per-root config-home candidate or name the gap in §Deferred beside `017-R2`.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "Steam Deck | Unknown" and "macOS | Unknown"
findings.problem: [new] The checklist admits no `unknown`: every row must commit, and both are decidable from evidence the design already cites. macOS is a definite No — crates/discovery/src/game.rs:21-28 publishes `Platform` as exactly SteamLinux/SteamWindows and apps/discovery-cli/src/main.rs:131-132 builds only those plugins, so no macOS row can ever reach `GameContext::from_record`; §Deferred already defers "the macOS Steam root" to `017-R2`, which contradicts calling the row unknown. The Deck is a Linux Steam install with the same `$HOME` layout and Proton prefix rule the Proton row claims Yes for; "no Deck leg exists (A22)" is a coverage fact, not a status.
findings.fix: Mark macOS `No — no macOS discovery source exists, so no row resolves` (pointing at `017-R2`), and Steam Deck `Yes, by the Linux row`, moving the no-Deck-fixture note into that row's Notes.

findings.location: Test strategy #16 — "the workspace `Cargo.lock` is unchanged" — and Rollout 9 — "any `Cargo.lock` change is a finding"
findings.problem: [new] These contradict the run's own gate. `Cargo.lock` records every workspace member (stanzas for bindforge-core, bindforge-transforms, discovery, discovery-cli at Cargo.lock:56,72,141,151), so landing `crates/codecs` necessarily adds a `bindforge-codecs` stanza plus the `apps/discovery-cli` → `bindforge-codecs` edge, and Rollout 9's own `cargo test --workspace --locked` fails while the lock is stale. As written the design makes its gate unsatisfiable and forces the implementer to break a stated rule.
findings.fix: Restate both places as the narrower claim the matrix row already makes: the only delta is the `bindforge-codecs` stanza and the `discovery-cli` dependency edge, with no new third-party package and no version moving; pin that instead.

findings.location: The CLI face, step 5 — "`EXIT_FAILURE` 1 (usage, undiscovered slug, scan failure — today's one voice) · `claim-refused` 2"
findings.problem: [new] Exit 1 is assigned to a class that never reaches this code: the binary parses through clap 4 (`Cli::parse()`, apps/discovery-cli/src/main.rs:73; `clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive"] }`, apps/discovery-cli/Cargo.toml:11), and clap exits 2 on a usage error before `main` runs. So `discovery bindings` with a missing `<slug>` or a misspelled flag exits 2 — the code reserved for `claim-refused` — breaking the section's own promise that "the code is a function of what stdout showed" and making Test strategy #13's (0/2/3/4) pins undecodable by consumers.
findings.fix: State that the face parses with `Cli::try_parse()` and routes the parse error through the existing `error: ` + `ExitCode::FAILURE` voice (main.rs:80-83) so usage stays 1; or move the four status codes above clap's 2 and say so in the same sentence.

findings.location: The first family fixture list / Test strategy #6 — "`symlinked-prefix`" … "a symlinked directory and a symlinked `.ini` in `symlinked-prefix` are neither descended nor read"
findings.problem: [new] The design never says how those links come to exist, and the likeliest route breaks the gate Rollout 9 promises: the Windows leg is `cargo check --workspace --exclude bindforge-registry --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (.github/workflows/check.yml:42-46), so `crates/codecs` test targets compile for that target, and a test-time `std::os::unix::fs::symlink` helper (this would be the repo's first symlink test — no existing file under crates/ calls `symlink`) does not compile there; a symlink checked into git is not a link in a Windows checkout.
findings.fix: One sentence pinning the mechanism: links created at test time behind `#[cfg(unix)]` with a `#[cfg(not(unix))]` early return so the compile leg stays green, and the assertion runs on the Linux leg only.

findings.location: `bindings/v1` bounds — "`user` one of the three spellings above"
findings.problem: [new] The contract never says whether the three labels are a closed set the loader refuses anything outside, or the set `v1` emits. Since `bindings/v1` ages through majors, this is a permanent commitment: `017-R2`'s Windows launcher context has a local user who is neither a SteamID nor `steamuser` nor `host`, so a closed enumeration forces either overloading `host` (losing the label) or a format major.
findings.fix: One sentence deciding it: the loader validates `user` against a bounded token grammar (the shared slug-shaped bound plus the section's control-character and space rules) and spec.md lists the spellings `v1` emits; or keep the closed set and state that a new launcher-context label is a `bindings` major.

findings.location: Read discipline and budgets — the `ExtractionRefusal` variant list "`FileOverBudget`, `UndecodableText`, `UnparsableEntry` … and `SnapshotEntryBudget`" — against `bindings/v1` bounds' "each input token the same bound"
findings.problem: [new] A located line whose verbatim `Command=` or `Name=` string exceeds `MAX_NATIVE_NAME_OCTETS` has no named outcome at the extraction seam: the format's over-bound refusal ("a value outside its bound is a refusal naming the key") governs a loaded document, while at extraction the family must drop the pair — which §Deferred forbids ("`v1` reports the file's tokens verbatim and drops nothing") — or refuse under a name the list does not carry, which `017-L1` forbids. UE's `Command` field is a free-form console command line, so this is real-file territory.
findings.fix: Name the outcome: state that an over-bound verbatim token is an `UnparsableEntry` carrying the bound's name with the tree-relative path and 1-based line, or add one variant; the status stays `extraction-refused`.

findings.location: Read discipline and budgets — "MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME = 16 | `userdata/` directories considered per game" with Test strategy #3's "a 17th digit-named directory is past `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME` and unvisited"
findings.problem: [new] This is the only budget in the design that ends in silent omission instead of a named outcome: on a machine with more local Steam users the run emits fewer documents with no status, refusal or stderr line, so an operator cannot tell "every user's bindings" from "the first sixteen" — where every other budget here names itself (`FileOverBudget`, `SnapshotEntryBudget`, the candidate cap).
findings.fix: One sentence deciding it: the cap is reported (a named line in the run's output, run still `ok`), or spec.md and the README budget bullet state it plainly as a silent bound on users per game.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — Windows host row: "no Windows tree template ships, so the face answers `claim-refused`"
findings.problem: [new] The stated reason misdescribes the behavior: `SteamUserdata` and `ProtonPrefix` are root-relative and OS-neutral, so on a Windows host with a discovered Steam row both templates are built and stat'd; `claim-refused` arrives because no `Saved/Config` grammar is located inside them, not because nothing resolves — the wrong failure model for whoever picks up `017-R2`.
findings.fix: Restate as: the root-relative trees resolve; no template ships for the Windows host config home (`%LOCALAPPDATA%`, `Documents\My Games`), so a real title answers `claim-refused`.

findings.location: The first family — "collecting `*.ini` files whose path ends `Saved/Config/<one directory>/<name>.ini`"
findings.problem: [new] The design does not say the match is component-wise; a suffix test against `path.display()` is separator-dependent, which is exactly where `017-R2`'s Windows trees will bite.
findings.fix: Add one clause: matched on `Path::components()` suffix components plus `file_name()` ending `.ini`, never on a displayed string.

findings.location: §Config-path resolvers (closing paragraph) and §Read discipline — "Candidate paths are never canonicalized: the anchors (`root`, `library`) are already canonical from the scan, and §Read discipline never descends a link, so no resolved path is needed to keep a walk inside a tree."
findings.problem: The no-link-descent rule only governs the walk below a UserTree root; the root itself is built by join and is opened with the OS following links. SteamUserdata's <dir> component is a read_dir name filtered solely by the 1–20-digit rule ("one per digit-named `<dir>`"), so a digit-named symlink under userdata/ is accepted as a tree root, and for ProtonPrefix the whole pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser chain is filesystem content that A17 says is "held together by symlinks". A symlinked tree anchor relocates the locate walk outside the context's trees, breaking 017-C2's "locates nothing outside the context's trees" (re-quoted in §GameContext) — the very containment claim used to justify skipping canonicalization. Test strategy #6 pins links inside the walk only, so implementation and suite both miss the anchor.
findings.fix: In §Config-path resolvers state that a UserTree is returned only when its final component is not a symlink (DirEntry::file_type() on enumerated userdata/<dir> entries; symlink_metadata on a template root), skipped and counted like a symlinked directory in the walk; replace the absolute claim "no resolved path is needed to keep a walk inside a tree" with the qualified one (no link is followed anywhere, anchor included) and extend the symlinked-prefix fixture and Test #6 with a symlinked tree root.

findings.location: §`bindings/v1` — "Bounds, stated once here and cited elsewhere: … `entries` ≤ `MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES`; `files` ≤ `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` per document."
findings.problem: One entry's `inputs` array has no count bound (only each token's octets are bounded), so entries × inputs is unbounded, and no constant in the five-constant budget family or in §bindings/v1 caps the byte size of a document the snapshot loader parses. The contract tree's posture is the opposite: schemas/README.md's "Input budget and chain bound (adversarial guard)" binds a 1 MiB cap before the read for documents arriving from disk, another user, or the network, every existing spec.md restates it, and every array-shaped field of every format carries a named bound (MAX_MANIFEST_ROWS, MAX_PATCH_DELTA_ELEMENTS, MAX_POLICY_TRANSFORMS, MAX_RELOCATE_TARGETS). The precedent this design copies, schemas/catalog/v1/spec.md, states MAX_CATALOG_DOCUMENT_OCTETS with an fs::metadata-gated pre-read check. bindings/v1 is built to travel to manifest authoring, the apply tool and UI import, and ages through majors, so a refusal added later breaks already-valid documents and the hole becomes permanent at implementation. Test strategy #10's invalid corpus and #15's README pin cover neither case.
findings.fix: Add one named per-entry input bound (MAX_INPUTS_PER_ENTRY) to the §Read discipline budget table, the schemas/README.md budget bullet and the aggregate sentence, and state in §bindings/v1 that the snapshot.rs loader applies a MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES-style fs::metadata length check before parsing (the same A4 posture §Read discipline uses); add one invalid fixture per bound to Test #10.

findings.location: §The first family — "collecting `*.ini` files whose path ends `Saved/Config/<one directory>/<name>.ini` and whose text carries a `[/Script/Engine.PlayerInput]` section with at least one `Bindings=` line"
findings.problem: Claiming requires opening and decoding game-owned files during detect, but only extract is routed through the reader ("extract reads only located files, through `read.rs`"), and the design never says what a path-grammar match that is over budget or undecodable does at locate time. The natural reading is a silent skip, which reports an over-budget or undecodable binding store as claim-refused/family-confirmed-files-absent — the distinction 017-L1 exists to keep ("a claimed game with an unreadable binding file is a different fact from a game no codec claimed") — and it is the one place a codec could allocate a file's whole body before MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS is consulted.
findings.fix: Add a clause stating that locate tests candidates through read::open_capped plus read::decode (which is also what makes the bom-utf16 fixture locatable), and that a path-grammar match that is over budget or undecodable claims and refuses by name (FileOverBudget / UndecodableText) rather than being skipped.

findings.location: §`bindings/v1` — "`user` (the context label, absent when the family's storage is not user-scoped)"
findings.problem: The spec's stated content list (key set, bounds, ordering law, refusal names) never records that one key carries a persistent personal identifier (the local SteamID) in a document intended to travel between tools and machines, so a later sharing surface inherits the disclosure silently.
findings.fix: One sentence in schemas/bindings/v1/spec.md naming `user` as launcher-local identity that any sharing surface must treat as personal data; behaviour unchanged.

findings.location: §Local paths (scoping) — "`--probe` mode exists to name files, so it prints absolute paths in probe output and tree-relative ones in the contract document"
findings.problem: The scoping argument holds against the rule it cites (schemas/README.md's no-path clause is scoped to a message shown to whoever sent the document), but probe lines also disclose the OS username and the SteamID, and the Risks row frames the exposure only as a reviewer expecting the no-path discipline.
findings.fix: Add that disclosure to the same paragraph (probe output is local-operator output, not safe to paste into a public issue) instead of changing the behaviour.

findings.location: §The first family / §Read discipline and budgets — "`detect` walks each `UserTree` depth-first in byte order to `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH`, collecting `*.ini` files whose path ends `Saved/Config/<one directory>/<name>.ini` ... capped at `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` per tree"
findings.problem: The cap bounds the result set, not the traversal, and two of the three UserTree roots are whole user-directory trees: `NativeHost` is "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME when set and absolute, else $HOME/.config" and `ProtonPrefix` is `<library>/steamapps/compatdata/<appid>/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser` (the entire emulated profile). The worst case is the zero-match case — a game the family does not have natively — where the walk descends the full tree to depth 8, calls `file_type()` on every entry, and never reaches the 32-file cap that would stop it early. No constant bounds directories or entries visited, so the command path carries an unbounded synchronous walk per invocation; the aggregate sentence counts only opened files and reads as a bound where none exists. This is a new cost shape: the shipped scan is shallow (one `read_dir` of `<library>/steamapps` at crates/discovery/src/steam_common.rs:195 plus size-capped VDF/ACF reads), so no existing posture already bounds a deep walk.
findings.fix: Add one design-time constant beside the other two (e.g. `MAX_LOCATE_ENTRIES_PER_TREE`: entries examined below a `UserTree` root, over-cap entries skipped and counted the way `steam_common`'s `skipped` counter already does, degrading to `family-confirmed-files-absent`), name it in the §Read discipline budget table and in the aggregate sentence, and add a prune clause: the grammar's four trailing components (`Saved/Config/<dir>/<name>.ini`) mean the walk need not descend a directory whose remaining depth budget is below that suffix.

findings.location: §`bindings/v1` / §Read discipline and budgets — "`entries` ≤ `MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES`" with table row "`MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES = 4096` | one snapshot's entries | `017-B2`", read against "Entries are keyed by the `Command` string verbatim ... and carry the distinct `Name` tokens verbatim as `inputs`"
findings.problem: The budget counts grouped actions, not bindings, so no constant bounds a snapshot's input-token count, pair count or serialized size. A 1 MiB INI is inside `MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS`, so no file budget fires; ~15,000 lines of `+Bindings=(Name="KEY_<n>",Command="Action")` produce one entry with 15,000 inputs, `SnapshotEntryBudget` never triggers, and across `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` per tree the in-memory token set is bounded only by bytes read. Peak is worse than one document because `extract` returns every user tree's snapshot at once (`Result<Vec<BindingSnapshot>, ExtractionRefusal>`) across up to 18 trees. `017-B2`'s purpose is the pair count ("a game with more bindings than this does not exist today"), and the Risks table names "five named budgets" as the mitigation for "Untrusted config files: enormous, deeply nested, UTF-16, symlinked out of the tree, over budget", which this unit choice defeats.
findings.fix: Define the `017-B2` count over distinct (action, input-token) pairs instead of `entries` array length — the same `SnapshotEntryBudget` check site evaluated on the pair total — and state in §`bindings/v1` that `entries` array length is additionally bounded by it. No new constant, no new refusal name.

findings.location: §Read discipline and budgets — "one extraction opens at most `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` files, so its worst-case read cost is `16 × 32 × MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS` (512 MiB) for one game, offline, one game at a time"
findings.problem: The product omits two of the three template families: `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME` bounds only the `SteamUserdata` trees, while `ProtonPrefix` and `NativeHost` each contribute one more tree with its own `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` budget, and `extract` returns one document per tree. The README amendment is instructed to copy this sentence ("states the aggregate product"), so `schemas/README.md`'s budget family would ship a ceiling understated by 64 files / 64 MiB. The figure also ignores the per-record multiplier: step 3 runs `from_record` → `claim` → `extract` "Per matching record" and "More than one record matching ... each is processed and rendered", so N matching records repeat the same `NativeHost` walk N times (that tree's root does not depend on the record's root or library).
findings.fix: State the product as `(MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 2) × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` files (576 at the current constants), naming the `+2` as the `ProtonPrefix` and `NativeHost` trees, plus one clause that the worst case multiplies by the number of matching records.

findings.location: §Discovery plumbing (`crates/discovery`) — "`src/steam_common.rs`: `SteamCore::scan()` returns `Vec<ScanRecord>`; `discover()` becomes `Ok(self.scan()?.into_iter().map(|r| r.game).collect())`"
findings.problem: The chosen seam threads per-row root ownership through the code path that produces `list`'s byte-pinned rows (`crates/discovery/src/steam_common.rs:90-130`), and that one choice generates the run's only High-impact compatibility risk ("The `steam_common` refactor changes what `list` prints"), Test strategy 1, Rollout 1's re-pin caveat, and a new cross-crate public type that `crates/discovery/tests/zz_api_probe.rs` does not name. It also hands `GameContext` a single owning root, which is not what `017-C2` asks for ("every steam root the scan resolved — main root and library roots separately") — an unregistered fourth divergence from the source wording, since the Context section registers only three.
findings.fix: Leave `discover()` untouched and add one read-only inherent accessor per Steam plugin returning the two sets the scan already computes (the canonicalized `SteamCore` roots, plus the existing `libraries_in_root_with_skips` at `steam_common.rs:137`, reachable only through that accessor because `mod steam_common;` is private at `lib.rs:6`); make `GameContext` carry `roots: Vec<PathBuf>` / `libraries: Vec<PathBuf>` and have `user_trees` de-duplicate resolved trees by path. This replaces the `ScanRecord` struct, the ownership-preserving rewrite of the shared `canonical_paths` dedupe, the two `scan_records()` wrappers, Test strategy 1 and the `list`-output Risk row, and satisfies `017-C2`'s wording literally instead of by ownership inference.

findings.location: §`bindings/v1` — Bounds — "`user` one of the three spellings above"
findings.problem: The contract validates a launcher-context vocabulary (1–20 digits | `steamuser` | `host`), turning the resolvers' internal knowledge into a format rule. `017-R2`'s Windows contexts, whose user directory is not `steamuser` (A17), then require a `bindings` major rather than a new resolver, and the loader carries a rule no Goal asks for. Test strategy 10's "a non-digit `user` under a userdata-shaped label" makes the coupling concrete: the document has no tree-kind key, so the rule is only implementable as this run's invented pattern union.
findings.fix: State `user` as an opaque label under the bounds every other string already rides (1–`MAX_NATIVE_NAME_OCTETS`, no control character, no leading/trailing space) and keep the three spellings as prose about the resolvers; delete the enumeration from the bounds and that one invalid fixture.

findings.location: §Read discipline and budgets — "`MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME = 16` … `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH = 8` … design-time"
findings.problem: These are the run's only two budgets without an ADR unit (the proposal says so), and no text establishes the values: the layouts they must cover are `unverified` in the register (A15, A17) and no surveyed layout depth or per-machine SteamID count is recorded. The property that cannot be established from the document is that `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH = 8` is at least the depth of the deepest layout the family claims to resolve — which is the sole reason the locate walk is generic rather than template-shaped.
findings.fix: Add one sentence beside each constant naming the deepest surveyed layout path (native, Proton, userdata) and the observed SteamID count per machine it was sized from, and extend Test strategy 6 to assert a miss at `surveyed_depth + 1`. Keep the constants; ground them.

findings.location: §Test strategy 16 and Rollout 9 — "and the workspace `Cargo.lock` is unchanged" / "any `Cargo.lock` change is a finding"
findings.problem: As worded the pin cannot pass: adding `crates/codecs` to the workspace necessarily changes `Cargo.lock` (a new `[[package]] bindforge-codecs` entry plus new edges from it and from `apps/discovery-cli`), and `serde_json` is not in `[workspace.dependencies]` (`Cargo.toml:20-24`), so the new crate declares it directly. The intended claim (A12: no new external crate, no version change) is true — `serde_json` is already resolved at `Cargo.lock:317` and the `crates/*` glob exists at `Cargo.toml:12`.
findings.fix: Restate both places as "the only `Cargo.lock` diff is the new member's own entry and its edges — no new external package and no version change", so the gate asserts the property that was meant.

findings.location: §`GameContext` — "`pub platform: discovery::game::Platform,`"
findings.problem: No rule in the design reads it: the three tree templates are anchored on `root`/`library`/env, and the Windows `claim-refused` answer comes from `from_record`'s digit-appid gate plus no located trees, not from the platform value.
findings.fix: Name the clause that consumes `platform`, or drop the field until `017-R2` needs it; `017-C2` asks for the row's identity parts, not its platform.

findings.location: §The CLI face — "the shared table renderer, generalized from `COLUMNS.len()` to a `&[String]` header so `list`'s five columns and their pinned widths are unchanged" alongside item 6's "`discovery list` is untouched"
findings.problem: The two sentences describe editing the renderer `list` renders through (`apps/discovery-cli/src/main.rs:377-420`, where `Row`/`Widths` are fixed-size arrays keyed to `COLUMNS`) while claiming `list` is untouched. Generalizing is the smaller option over a second width algorithm; only the claim is wrong.
findings.fix: Say "`list`'s rendering code is refactored to slice widths with byte-identical output, pinned by `cli_output_polish_tests` and `cli_json_mode_tests`" instead of "untouched".

reply.summary: Round 1 consumed by changing the design, not appending to it. Correctness 1 + compatibility 1 + performance 1/3 + the CLI duplicate-document tie: the `NativeHost` tree and its `env` lookup closure are deleted — no host-config tree ships (`$HOME/.config` is not game-scoped and no `ScanRecord` field names the UE project directory), the context now supplies no environment at all, both remaining templates hang off a resolved root (Flatpak/Snap, Windows-host and Linux rows restated honestly), and the native context moves to §Deferred as a recorded `017-S1` divergence. Correctness 2: `GameContext` carries `roots: Vec<PathBuf>` (017-C2's whole resolved set, fed by a new `roots()` wrapper), and the "userdata/ lives here (A18)" assertion plus A18's design tail are gone. Correctness 3 + Determinism: `user_trees(ctx)` takes the context alone and the law now names the process environment. Correctness 4 + compatibility 3: the `Cargo.lock` claim is stated once in §`crates/codecs` as the `bindforge-codecs` stanza plus the `discovery-cli` edge, and #16 and Rollout 9 are narrowed to match. Correctness 5 + performance 3: the aggregate is `(MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 1) × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` (544 files) times matching records. Correctness 6: UE's four operators (`+`, `.`, `-`, `!`) replace three with `.` misdescribed, in the fold and in #7. Correctness 7: the `extract`-returns-a-document-per-tree divergence gets its Revision-log entry and its unit id in Rollout 8. Compatibility 2: macOS is a committed `No`, the Deck `Yes, by the Linux row`. Compatibility 4: the status codes moved to 3/4/5, leaving clap's usage 2 alone (#13 renumbered). Compatibility 5/6/7/8: `#[cfg(unix)]` link fixtures with a compile-only arm, `user` validated by token grammar rather than a closed label list, an over-bound verbatim token named as the existing `UnparsableEntry`, and `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME` declared a silent bound. Security 1–3 + performance 1: a `UserTree` whose final component is a link is skipped and counted, locate reads through `read::open_capped`/`read::decode` and refuses by name, `MAX_LOCATE_ENTRIES_PER_TREE` ceilings the walk, and the loader's `fs::metadata` check rides `MAX_SNAPSHOT_OCTETS`; the `user` personal-data sentence and the probe-username/SteamID disclosure are added. Performance 2: `017-B2` now counts (`action`, input-token) pairs. Nits: OpenOptions spelling, boundary-sweep skip set, `Path::components()` matching, `cargo deny` in the gate list, concrete plugin typing noted. Diff is net positive because the round retired one of three tree families but added three named budget constants, a roots seam and fixture/cfg provisions that four seats demanded, which cannot be absorbed by deletion alone.
reply.commitMessage: docs: revise ADR-017 proposal for round 1 design review

findings.location: Determinism (`017-L4`) — canonical — "across documents, deduplicated by (`user`, `provenance.files`) — two records that resolve the same tree state it once — then byte order by `user`" (with §The CLI face step 3 and Test strategy #12)
findings.problem: new (created by the round-1 duplicate-document closure): the dedup key is weaker than tree identity, so it merges documents from *different* trees whenever they share a `user` label and tree-relative paths — the normal shape of the multi-library case §The CLI face step 3 explicitly supports: one game in two libraries yields two `ProtonPrefix` trees whose `user` is the constant `steamuser` with the same tree-relative Windows path, and two resolved roots each holding `<same steamid>/<same appid>` yield two `SteamUserdata` trees with the same `user` and the same relative files. The dropped tree's located files then appear in no document's `provenance.files` and its bindings are silently lost — against §`bindings/v1`'s own "One JSON document per game per located user tree", against `017-C3`'s per-user document rule, and against `017-L3`, while `--probe` still prints those files as located. The key also fails to finish what it was added for: surviving same-`user` documents from distinct trees still tie under "byte order by `user`", so #12's byte-identity premise is unpinned. No test catches the over-merge — #12's "two records that resolve the same user tree yield one document" passes under the wrong key too.
findings.fix: Key the dedup on the resolved `UserTree` anchor path (identity, never rendered) together with (`user`, `provenance.files`), so a tree is stated once per tree and two distinct trees under one label stay two documents; break the surviving `user` tie in the law by byte order over the serialized document; add one fixture (one slug in two libraries, two prefixes with different `Bindings`) asserting two documents and two `--probe` groups.

findings.location: Read discipline and budgets — `src/read.rs` — "one extraction opens at most `(MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 1) × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` files — the `+1` is the `ProtonPrefix` tree" (with §Config-path resolvers' "for every `root` in `ctx.roots` … at most `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME`" and the table's "userdata/ directories considered per game")
findings.problem: new: the §GameContext closure made `SteamUserdata` a union over `ctx.roots`, but no constant bounds `ctx.roots` — verified at `crates/discovery/src/steam_common.rs:77-82,369-381`: `with_roots` keeps the whole `host_candidates` list (10 candidates on Linux, `steam_linux.rs:92-128`) filtered only to installs that exist — so the tree count is `≤ MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME × |ctx.roots| + 1` and the aggregate that `schemas/README.md` is told to publish understates the worst case by the root count. The resolver sentence also reads as a per-root cap while the constant's Bounds column says per game, leaving Test #3's "a 17th digit-named directory is past `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME` and unvisited" ambiguous as to 17th within one root or across the union.
findings.fix: State that `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME` caps the *union*: the `user_trees` pass takes the distinct digit-named `<dir>` names across all of `ctx.roots` and stops at the 16th — which makes the `(MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 1) × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` product true as written and makes #3 unambiguous.

findings.location: Discovery plumbing — `crates/discovery` — "`SteamLinuxPlugin`/`SteamWindowsPlugin` expose `scan_records()` and `roots()` (the selected root candidates, in candidate order) as thin inherent wrappers" (with §`GameContext`'s "`pub roots: Vec<PathBuf>,  // every root the scan resolved, candidate order`" and §Discovery plumbing's "libraries are enumerated per root in root-candidate order")
findings.problem: new: "candidate order" is false of what a thin wrapper reads. `SteamCore::with_roots` replaces the candidate list with `canonical_paths(roots)` (`steam_common.rs:77-82`), which drops entries that fail to canonicalize or lack a `steamapps` directory and returns a `BTreeSet` — canonicalized, existence-filtered, byte-sorted (`:369-381`). The seam the design hands `GameContext.roots` therefore cannot deliver the order the comment and the enumeration sentence state, and Test #2 ("yields … every resolved root") pins a field whose stated order does not exist.
findings.fix: Say what the seam holds: "`roots()` returns the selected roots as the core holds them — canonicalized, existence-filtered, byte order — and `GameContext.roots` carries that order", replacing both "candidate order" claims.

findings.location: The first family — `src/families/unreal_ini.rs` — "`!` removes by name" beside "`-` removes on an exact match", with "blank lines and out-of-grammar lines in a section are skipped"
findings.problem: new: the newly accepted operator's operand grammar is unpinned, and the spelling the cited UE doc actually documents is the bare property form (verified live at A15's URL: "`!` — Removes a property; but you do not have to have an exact match, just the name of the property"). `!Bindings=` carries no tuple, so under this section's rules it is neither a `Bindings=(…)` tuple (the `UnparsableEntry` clause) nor an accepted pair line and falls to "out-of-grammar lines … are skipped": a binding set the file cleared keeps being reported — the same silent drift round 1 raised `!` to close. `!Bindings=` and `!Bindings=(Name="Q")` have no stated difference.
findings.fix: One clause replacing the bare "`!` removes by name": "`!Key=` with no value clears every pair accumulated for that key in the working set; `!Key=<tuple>` removes the pairs the tuple names" — and name both spellings in Test #7.

findings.location: Assumption register A15 — "its `Input`/`PlayerInput` category carries `Bindings=(Name=…,Command=…)` lines with documented `+`/`-`/`.` merge operators"
findings.problem: new in changed text: the register still enumerates three operators while §The first family now decides four and the Revision log records "the fold keeps UE's four merge operators (`+`, `.`, `-`, `!`)". The A15 basis URL lists exactly four (`+`, `-`, `.`, `!`), so the row understates the basis its own citation supports and the register and the body disagree about the grammar's extent.
findings.fix: Add `!` to A15's enumeration in place — one character and its wording, no new row.

findings.location: `bindings/v1` — the snapshot contract — "Bounds, stated once here and cited elsewhere: … `files` ≤ `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES`; the document ≤ `MAX_SNAPSHOT_OCTETS`"
findings.problem: new: the rewritten bounds list gives every other string in the closed key set a length bound (`codec`, `game`, `action`, every input token, `user`) but gives `provenance.files` entries only a count, so a contract `017-C3` requires to keep "every string … inside the shared bounds" ships one unbounded string field guarded only by the whole-document read cap; Test #10's refusal-by-name list consequently has no over-bound `files` case.
findings.fix: Bound each `files` entry with one named constant stated once here (the locate walk's own ceiling — `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH` components — is its honest home), and add the over-bound path to #10's refusal list.

findings.location: Rollout item 8 **Ledger** — "the units whose shipped reading differs from their wording (`017-C1`'s bound and `extract` return shape, `017-C3`'s `inputs`, `017-C4`'s "same scan", `017-S1`'s launcher contexts)", with §Context's "Five clauses of the source are read differently than worded"
findings.problem: new: the Risks row states the run's own rule — "Each divergence is a Revision-log entry with its basis, the unit ids are listed for the operator's ledger annotation (§Rollout item 8)" — but two Revision-log decisions reinterpret source units and are in neither the five-clause count nor this hand-off: §GameContext's "`roots` is `017-C2`'s whole resolved set, so `userdata/` is found under the install that owns the game, not a 'main' one", which contradicts `017-C2`'s "every steam root the scan resolved — main root and library roots separately, because `userdata/` lives only under the main root"; and §Read discipline's "`017-B2` counts (`action`, input-token) pairs" against `017-B2`'s "the cap on one snapshot's entries". On a `ledger: yes` ADR the operator's `amended-by` lines are the only record of what shipped, and §Context's count is what the operator reconciles against. The §GameContext entry is also labelled "Initial:" though it is a round-1 change.
findings.fix: Add `017-C2`'s root labelling and `017-B2`'s pair reading to Rollout 8's hand-off list and to §Context's count (seven), and relabel the §GameContext log entry `R1:`.

findings.location: The first family — `detect` — "never descending a directory whose remaining depth is under the grammar's four trailing components"
findings.problem: "remaining depth" is undefined against `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH`'s own definition ("directory levels the locate walk descends below a `UserTree` root"), and the natural reading (prune when `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH − current depth < 4`) refuses to descend past level 4 and so cannot reach the depths 6–8 that Test strategy #6 pins as found ("found at depth ≤ 8 and not at depth 9").
findings.fix: State the prune against the candidate rather than the walk: "a directory at level *d* below the tree root is descended only while a `Saved/Config/<dir>/<name>.ini` can still complete by level `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH`".

findings.location: The first family — `detect` — "opened through `read::open_capped` and `read::decode`, so an over-budget or undecodable match claims and refuses by name rather than going unseen"
findings.problem: `detect` returns `Option<Detection>` and has no refusal channel, so the promise needs the locating rule spelled out: a file that fails `open_capped`/`decode` cannot also satisfy "holding a `[/Script/Engine.PlayerInput]` section with a `Bindings=` line", so as written it is unlocated and the refusal the sentence promises never happens.
findings.fix: One clause: a path-grammar match that fails `open_capped`/`decode` is located on path grammar alone and refused later by `extract` by name, while a decodable file without the section is not located.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — Steam Deck row — "A Linux Steam install with the `$HOME` and Proton prefix layout the two rows above claim"
findings.problem: no shipped resolver builds anything from `$HOME` (§Config-path resolvers: "No host-config tree ships this run"; §Deferred carries it), and the two rows above claim exactly the opposite for the host config home ("a host-config title answers `claim-refused`"); the row is right that the Linux row covers the Deck, but the layout it names is not one this run resolves.
findings.fix: "the root-relative `userdata/` and Proton prefix layout the two rows above claim, with the host config home deferred as they state".

findings.location: §Discovery plumbing + §GameContext — "`roots()` (the selected root candidates, in candidate order)" / "`pub roots: Vec<PathBuf>,  // every root the scan resolved, candidate order`"
findings.problem: [new] The order is false of the field the inherent wrapper would expose: `SteamCore` holds its roots through `canonical_paths` (crates/discovery/src/steam_common.rs:369-381), which canonicalizes (resolving symlink aliases such as `~/.steam/root`), drops entries that fail to canonicalize or lack a `steamapps/` directory, and returns a byte-sorted, de-duplicated set — not the candidate list. Test strategy #3 already says "the byte-order union over `ctx.roots`", so the design contradicts itself about the order an implementer must produce.
findings.fix: In both places state "the canonicalized, de-duplicated roots that actually hold a `steamapps/`, in byte order (the set `SteamCore` retains, steam_common.rs:369-381)" and drop "candidate order"; keep the existence-filter half as the reason "a tree is used only if it exists" is already true.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "Flatpak / Snap Steam | Yes, for the root-relative trees" and "Steam Deck | Yes, by the Linux row"
findings.problem: [new] Both rows were upgraded to Yes this round and both rest on the new `roots()` seam, which no test reaches: #1 pins `ScanRecord.root`/`library`, #2 pins only that `from_record` carries the slice it was handed, #3 pins the union over `ctx.roots`. No test or fixture is shaped like a Flatpak/Snap or Deck root, so the upgraded commitments are covered only by a structural test of the generic mechanism (checklist item 7).
findings.fix: One clause in #1 or #2 — `roots()` returns exactly what `SteamCore::with_roots` kept — and one `ctx.roots` entry in #3 shaped `~/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/.local/share/Steam` that yields a `SteamUserdata` tree. No discovery-side work is implied: the candidate list is already pinned at crates/discovery/tests/steam_linux_tests.rs:294-345.

findings.location: §Read discipline and budgets — "`MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME = 16` | `userdata/` directories considered per game" against §Config-path resolvers' "`<root>/userdata/<dir>/<ctx.appid>` for every `root` in `ctx.roots`, one per digit-named `<dir>`, byte order, at most `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME`"
findings.problem: [new] Making the template a union over roots leaves the cap's unit undecided — sixteen per game in total or per root — and the aggregate sentence counts only one set of sixteen ("`(MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 1) × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` … (544 MiB)"). Under the per-root reading, A3's nine Linux candidates plus any number of repeated `--steam-root` values put the worst case at `(|roots| × 16 + 1) × 32` files, several multiples of the figure `schemas/README.md`'s budget bullet is told to state.
findings.fix: One clause deciding it: the cap counts `userdata/` directories across all `ctx.roots` for one game (so the arithmetic stands), and say which directories are dropped when the union exceeds it. (Shared with the performance seat.)

findings.location: §Determinism + §The CLI face step 3 — "across documents, deduplicated by (`user`, `provenance.files`) — two records that resolve the same tree state it once"
findings.problem: [new] The key is sound for one game in two libraries, not for the roots union introduced in the same round: two distinct resolved roots can each carry `userdata/<same SteamID>/<appid>/` (native install plus a Flatpak or Snap Steam on one account), and since `files` are deliberately tree-relative ("the portability rule: the same layout states the same document on any machine"), those two trees share the key and one document is silently dropped — no refusal, no status, and no printed path that says which install answered.
findings.fix: Deduplicate at the `UserTree` level on the tree's absolute root path (which is exactly what the two-records case repeats) and let §The CLI face emit one document per distinct tree; same one-fact-stated-once property, without building document identity out of values the contract strips machine context from.

findings.location: §Rollout item 9 — "`cargo deny check advisories`, and `npm ci && npm run check` in `tools/orchestration`, per `.github/workflows/check.yml`"
findings.problem: [new] That leg is not one of the run's cargo gates: the workflow runs it as the separate ADR-027 `advisory-gate` job, which builds its own `cargo-deny` 0.20.2 from source on toolchain 1.88.0 inside a 30-minute budget precisely because it is "too heavy for the 15-minute `rust` job" (check.yml:83-126). A22's own enumeration of CI ("the cargo trio plus a Windows *compile* check … and the Node check") does not count it, and this run adds no external package for it to screen; listing it inside the run's gate set imports a tool install no other part of the design owns.
findings.fix: Either cite it as what it is — "the `advisory-gate` job, its own pinned scanner and toolchain; nothing here adds a package for it" — or keep A22's list; the same line could also name the `cargo check -p bindforge-registry --all-targets` step the `rust` job does run.

findings.location: §Rollout item 8 (Ledger) — "the units whose shipped reading differs from their wording (`017-C1`'s bound and `extract` return shape, `017-C3`'s `inputs`, `017-C4`'s 'same scan', `017-S1`'s launcher contexts)"
findings.problem: [new] `017-C2` is missing, although the Revision log already records a divergence from it ("§GameContext — `roots` is `017-C2`'s whole resolved set … not a 'main' one") and the ADR clause reads "every steam root the scan resolved — main root and library roots separately, because `userdata/` lives only under the main root". What ships is one undifferentiated `roots` vector with none labelled main, i.e. a shipped reading that differs from the wording, and this hand-off is the only mechanism that keeps the operator-owned `docs/adrs/` accurate.
findings.fix: Add `017-C2`'s main/library separation to the hand-off list and to the "Five clauses" count in §Context and the matching Risks row.

findings.location: §Goals — "`unreal-ini` ships with fixture trees for the two launcher contexts whose roots a record can justify"
findings.problem: [new] ADR-017's Terminology fixes a launcher context as "the native host layout, or the Proton prefix the game was launched under", so after this round's removal of the host template the two shipped trees (`steam-userdata`, `proton-prefix`) are not the ADR's two contexts, and the phrase hides that the native context is exactly what moved to §Deferred.
findings.fix: Reword to "the two root-relative trees a record can justify", with the context named where §Deferred already names it.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix, Steam Deck row — "A Linux Steam install with the `$HOME` and Proton prefix layout the two rows above claim"
findings.problem: [new] Nothing hangs off `$HOME` any more (§Config-path resolvers: "each built from a `GameContext` anchor and nothing else — no resolver reads the process environment"); the resolved Steam roots merely live under it, so the row describes a layout the design no longer claims.
findings.fix: "the root-relative `userdata/` and Proton prefix layout the Linux and Proton rows claim; unexercised here — no Deck leg (A22) and no Deck fixture".

findings.location: §Config-path resolvers (closing paragraph) — "Candidate paths are never canonicalized: the anchors (`roots`, `library`) are already canonical from the scan and no link is followed at an anchor or below one, so a walk never leaves the tree it started in."
findings.problem: re-raised (narrowed; the r1 major is otherwise closed). The named checks — `DirEntry::file_type()` on the enumerated `<dir>`, `symlink_metadata` on a template root — establish only that the tree root's final component is not a link; the joined template path can still carry a link at an intermediate component below the canonical anchor (`userdata` for SteamUserdata; `pfx`/`drive_c`/`users` for ProtonPrefix), which the OS follows during the join, anchoring the locate walk in an outside tree while the new sentence claims that is impossible. A17 itself records prefix trees as "held together by symlinks", so an intermediate link is the documented real-world shape, and Test #6 pins only `.ini`, directory and tree-root links, so the case is untested. Exploitation needs write access to the launcher's own trees and yields a grammar-filtered read of `.ini` files outside the context's trees with a bounded echo through `UnparsableEntry`/snapshot tokens — hence minor, not major.
findings.fix: Extend the existing check up the fixed template chain in one clause: every path component between the canonical anchor and the tree root is `symlink_metadata`-checked, and a link at any of them skips-and-counts the tree exactly as a linked final component already does (template paths are ≤ 6 components, so no unbounded work); add one `#[cfg(unix)]` link at a template-intermediate component to the `symlinked-prefix` fixture and assert it in Test #6.

findings.location: §The first family — "examining at most `MAX_LOCATE_ENTRIES_PER_TREE` entries per tree and never descending a directory whose remaining depth is under the grammar's four trailing components"
findings.problem: The new prune compares the remaining depth budget against the constant 4 without the case where the directory being descended is itself one of the grammar's named components (`Saved`, `Config`, the platform directory), where the components still needed below it are 3, 2 or 1. With `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH = 8` the rule stops descending at relative depth 5, so a candidate at relative depth 6–8 whose `Saved` sits at relative depth 2–5 is never enumerated. The design's own flagship Proton layout is that shape: the `ProtonPrefix` root `<ctx.library>/steamapps/compatdata/<ctx.appid>/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser` holds a packaged UE title's config at `AppData/Local/<Project>/Saved/Config/<Platform>/<Game>.ini` (relative depth 7), and the walk must descend `Config` at relative depth 5, where `8 − 5 = 3 < 4` prunes it. That title answers no-claim / `family-confirmed-files-absent` for the layout the row exists to serve, and Test strategy 6's pin "the `Saved/Config/<dir>/` grammar is found at depth ≤ 8 and not at depth 9" is false for it.
findings.fix: Delete the clause — `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH` plus the newly added `MAX_LOCATE_ENTRIES_PER_TREE` already bound the walk, which was the point of round 1's finding 1 — or restate it name-anchored: a directory at relative depth `d` need not be descended only when neither its own name nor any name within the three levels above it is one of the grammar's components, so the surviving prune costs no locatable file.

findings.location: §The first family / §Read discipline and budgets — "A candidate is an `*.ini` whose `Path::components()` end in `Saved/Config/<one directory>/<name>.ini` … holding a `[/Script/Engine.PlayerInput]` section with a `Bindings=` line, capped at `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` per tree and opened through `read::open_capped` and `read::decode`"
findings.problem: The content test is part of candidacy, so every path-grammar match must be opened and decoded before it can be counted as a candidate; the 32-file cap bounds the retained set, not the opens, and after this revision the only thing bounding opens is `MAX_LOCATE_ENTRIES_PER_TREE = 16_384`. Worst case is 16,384 opens of up to `MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS` each per tree (≈16 GiB), across up to 17 trees per game, against the figure §Read discipline instructs `schemas/README.md` to copy: "one extraction opens at most `(MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 1) × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` files … (544 MiB)". The shipped budget-family ceiling is understated by up to ~512× per tree — round 1's result-not-work shape relocated from the walk leg to the content-probe leg — and nothing refuses, since `detect` returns `Option<Detection>`, so the cost `017-L1` calls untrusted input is paid silently.
findings.fix: Gate the opens with the constant that exists: "at most `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` path-grammar matches per tree are opened and content-tested, in the walk's byte order; a further match is skipped and counted the way an entry past `MAX_LOCATE_ENTRIES_PER_TREE` is". The located set, byte order and §Determinism are untouched and the aggregate product becomes the actual open ceiling (ADR-017 Rollout 5: "budgets enforced at read and locate time").

findings.location: §Config-path resolvers / §Read discipline and budgets — "`SteamUserdata`: `<root>/userdata/<dir>/<ctx.appid>` for every `root` in `ctx.roots`, one per digit-named `<dir>`, byte order, at most `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME`"
findings.problem: This revision moved `userdata/` off a single anchor onto a `Vec` no constant bounds (`crates/discovery/src/steam_linux.rs:92-128` passes every candidate to `SteamCore::with_roots`, so a native plus Flatpak plus Snap install resolves about ten roots), and the sentence does not say whether `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME` caps the union over all roots or the directories found under each root. Test strategy 3's "byte-order union over `ctx.roots`" and "a 17th digit-named directory is past `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME`" imply the union — the only reading under which the aggregate's 17-tree term holds; the per-root reading makes the ceiling copied into `schemas/README.md` wrong by the roots factor.
findings.fix: Make the scope explicit in the same clause — "at most `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME` `SteamUserdata` trees in total across all `ctx.roots`" — and mirror it in that constant's Bounds cell, so the shipped number is derivable from the budget table alone.

findings.location: §Read discipline and budgets / §`bindings/v1` — "`SnapshotEntryBudget` on the pair total" and "the (`action`, input-token) pair total ≤ `MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES`, which bounds `entries` and every `inputs` array"

findings.fix: One clause in §Read discipline: the check runs as each pair enters the tree's working set, so the fold stops at `MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES + 1` pairs and names itself; Test strategy 4's two breach shapes then read as one mechanism. No new constant, no new refusal name.

reply.summary: All 13 open findings consumed, mostly by deletion or rewrite: the depth-prune clause is deleted (correctness nit + performance major 1) and the walk is now bounded by depth and entry count alone; opens are gated at MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES per tree in walk order, with the aggregate sentence restated so the published product is the real open ceiling (perf major 2); the cross-document dedup is re-keyed on the UserTree anchor path and the redundant `byte order by user` clause deleted, with §Config-path resolvers' tree order made total and a two-library fixture added to #12 (correctness major); MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME is stated as capping trees across all ctx.roots in the resolver bullet, the budget table's Bounds cell and Test #3 (both seats' minor); roots()' order is now what the core actually holds and `candidate order` is gone (correctness minor); a bare `!Key=` clears the key and `!Key=<tuple>` names pairs, with both spellings in Test #7, and A15 gains `!` (correctness minors); each provenance.files entry is bounded by MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH components with the case added to #10; a reader-refused match is located on path grammar alone and refused later by extract; SnapshotEntryBudget's check site is the working-set fold at MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES + 1 (perf minor 4); §Context and Rollout item 8 now carry the same seven-unit ledger list and the §GameContext log entry is relabelled R1; the Deck matrix row names the root-relative layout with the host config home deferred. findings.location: Determinism (`017-L4`) — canonical + The codec face — "across documents, deduplicated by the `UserTree.root` path each was built from — tree identity, never rendered" (with §The CLI face step 3's "§Determinism's dedup by tree identity keeps one tree stated once" and Test strategy #12's "with the registry and the `UserTree` vector shuffled in the test harness, yields byte-identical documents")

Neither the face that performs the cross-record dedup at step 3 nor the ordering law can see a document's `UserTree.root` — the round-1 key (`user`, `provenance.files`) was exactly what the payload exposes, and the replacement key is absent from it. findings.location: Determinism + `bindings/v1` + Test strategy #12 — "two distinct trees that share a `user` label stay two documents" (with §`bindings/v1`'s "One JSON document per game per located user tree" and #12's "two `ProtonPrefix` trees sharing the `steamuser` label with different bindings — yield two documents")
findings.problem: new: document identity is now the located tree, which is a reading of `017-C3`'s "one document per game per local SteamID where user-scoped" that the run's own divergence record does not carry — §Context's seven clauses name `017-C3`'s "`inputs` spelling" only, and the Revision-log entry that speaks to document count still gives the basis "`017-C3`'s per-user rule wins", which is now the opposite of what ships. Consequence beyond the ledger on a `ledger: yes` source: two documents can share every identity field a consumer can read (`codec`, `game`, `user`) while differing in `entries`, with identical tree-relative `provenance.files`, so `--json` shows an unlabelled pair of same-user documents.
findings.fix: Keep the per-tree rule and make the record true: reword that Revision-log entry's basis to "read differently than `017-C3`'s per-local-SteamID wording", name `017-C3`'s document-identity clause in §Context's count and §Rollout item 8's hand-off list, and add one clause to §`bindings/v1` stating that a consumer distinguishes same-`user` documents by nothing in the contract and must union their entries.

findings.location: The first family — `src/families/unreal_ini.rs` `extract` — "a bare `!Key=` (no value) clears every pair accumulated for that key, `!Key=<tuple>` removes only the pairs it names" (with §`bindings/v1`'s "`inputs` may be empty when the file's own merge operators removed every input for an action" and "the (`action`, input-token) pair total ≤ `MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES`, which bounds `entries`", Options' "record every distinct (native action, native input) pair … grouped by action", and §Read discipline's "`SnapshotEntryBudget`, checked as each pair enters a tree's working set")
findings.problem: new: the fold still does not say whether an action whose pairs have all been removed survives as an entry with `inputs: []`, and the cited passages answer opposite ways — §`bindings/v1`'s allowance says it survives, Options(b) derives entries from the surviving pair set so an action with no pairs contributes nothing. The newly added bare-clear is the operation that makes this the common case, and it decides the budget: if emptied actions survive and the mid-fold check counts the current working-set size, a churn file (add 4096, remove 4096, add 4096 others) passes the check and ships more than `MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES` entries, so "which bounds `entries`" is false.
findings.fix: One clause in §The first family — "a `Command` whose pairs are all removed leaves no entry" (then delete §`bindings/v1`'s empty-`inputs` allowance and its "never for any other reason" tail), or the mirror of it — plus three words in §Read discipline fixing the check to distinct pairs admitted; and name the bare operand for the other operators in the same sentence and in Test #7: "`-Bindings=`, `+Bindings=` and `.Bindings=` with no value are out-of-grammar and skipped", which the new bare-`!` form otherwise leaves open.

findings.location: `bindings/v1` — the snapshot contract — "`files` ≤ `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES`, each entry at most `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH` path components — the locate walk's own ceiling" (with §Read discipline's table row "`MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH = 8` | directory levels the locate walk descends below a `UserTree` root" and Test strategy #6's "found at depth ≤ 8 and not at depth 9")
findings.problem: new: the bound borrowed a constant whose only definition counts directory levels, while the bound itself counts path components, and nothing in the document defines the depth of a file. Under the table's definition a file eight directory levels below the tree root has nine tree-relative components, so `detect` legitimately locates a file whose entry the loader then refuses — Test #10 ("a `files` entry over `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH` components") and Test #11 ("documents produced by the family all pass the loader") cannot both hold. The fixture layouts sit at that boundary: `Documents/My Games/<Project>/Saved/Config/<Platform>/<name>.ini` is seven components under a Proton prefix root.
findings.fix: State the units once, in the candidate's terms — "a located file's tree-relative path is at most `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH` components, its last four being the grammar's `Saved/Config/<dir>/<name>.ini`" — and make #6 say "found at ≤ `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH` components and not beyond" instead of an undefined "depth".

findings.location: Config-path resolvers — `src/paths.rs` — "one per digit-named `<dir>` in byte order, at most `MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME` such trees in total across all roots" (with the section's return order "in `TreeKind` declaration order then byte order of the tree's `root`" and Test strategy #3's "a 17th tree over all of `ctx.roots`")
findings.problem: new: the cap is now stated over the union, but the order in which the 16th tree is reached is not, and the bullet runs two orders at once — the enumeration reads as roots-then-directory, the return order is byte order of the full tree path, and those disagree for prefix-adjacent roots (byte order puts `/home/a-b/userdata/…` before `/home/a/userdata/…` because `-` < `/`, while `roots()` byte order puts `/home/a` first). Which users the silent bound keeps is therefore open, and #3 does not pin it.
findings.fix: Name the cut order in that bullet — "the cap is applied while enumerating `ctx.roots` in `roots()` order and `<dir>` in byte order; the surviving trees are then returned in `root` byte order" — and state which two roots and directories #3's fixture uses.

findings.location: §Read discipline and budgets — "since §The first family caps a tree's reads at `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` the product also ceilings the *opens*, so the worst case is `17 × 32 × MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS` (544 MiB) per game"
findings.problem: The aggregate counts one open pass per tree, but the family performs two: `detect` opens every path-grammar match through `read::open_capped` and `read::decode` for the content test, and `extract` then "reads only located files, through `read.rs`" — necessarily a second open pass, since the claim payload is `UserCandidates { user: String, files: Vec<PathBuf> }` (paths, not bytes). Worst case per game is 2 × (MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 1) × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES opens (1088) and ≈1.1 GiB read, against the figure this section instructs `schemas/README.md` to copy into its budget family (544 opens / 544 MiB) — the shipped aggregate is 2× low, in the repo's only place where a read cost is stated as a number, and the precedent shape it cites (`MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH × MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES`, schemas/README.md:132-133) is exact rather than approximate. Residue of round 1's finding 2, narrowed from 512× to 2× by the new cap.
findings.fix: One clause naming both legs: "detect's content test and extract's fold are two open passes over the same ≤ `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` set, so the face reads at most `2 × (MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 1) × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES × MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS` (1.1 GiB) per game" — or replace §The first family's "`extract` reads only located files, through `read.rs`" with `UserCandidates` carrying each located file's decoded bytes so extract never re-opens, making the single-pass figure true at the cost of retaining up to `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES × MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS` per tree. Either keeps the budget table, constants and refusal names unchanged.

findings.location: §`bindings/v1` Bounds with the §Read discipline table row — "`files` ≤ `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES`, each entry at most `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH` path components — the locate walk's own ceiling" vs "`MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH = 8` | directory levels the locate walk descends below a `UserTree` root"
findings.problem: The two bounds are stated in different units and differ by one. A file in a directory at the deepest legal descent has 8 directory components plus its own name = 9 path components, so the refusal Test strategy 10 pins ("a `files` entry over `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH` components") fires on a located file Test strategy 6 says the walk finds ("the `Saved/Config/<dir>/` grammar is found at depth ≤ 8"), and Test strategy 11's "documents produced by the family all pass the loader" cannot hold at that boundary — in the one clause whose stated purpose ("the locate walk's own ceiling") is to make the contract bound derivable from the walk. Minor because the layouts this family serves are 6–7 components deep, so the gap sits at the cap's edge, not on a shipped path.
findings.fix: State the unit once in the table row: "directory levels the locate walk descends below a `UserTree` root, so a located file's tree-relative path has at most `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH` components counting the file itself (a file in the root is 1)" — or restate the contract bound as `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH + 1` components.
