findings.location: §Read discipline and budgets — "since §The first family caps a tree's reads at `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` the product also ceilings the *opens*, so the worst case is `17 × 32 × MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS` (544 MiB) per game"
findings.problem: [re-raised, unchanged text — not a regression, does not bear on ratification] This sentence and the structure behind it were untouched by the revisions, so the shipped aggregate remains 2× low: §The first family opens every path-grammar match through `read::open_capped` and `read::decode` for `detect`'s content test, and `extract` then "reads only located files, through `read.rs`" — a second open pass, since `UserCandidates` still carries `files: Vec<PathBuf>` (the new `tree_root: PathBuf` is an ordering key, "never rendered into a document", not bytes). Worst case per game is 2 × (MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 1) × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES opens (1088) and ≈1.1 GiB read, in the repo's only place a read cost is stated as a number, which §Contract-tree amendments item 1 has `schemas/README.md` copy; the precedent shape cited (`schemas/README.md:131-133`, `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH × MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES` (32 MiB), verified) is exact for a single pass. The R1 Revision-log entry restates what the aggregate counts ("the aggregate counts every tree") and so does not rebut the pass count.

findings.location: §Read discipline budget table — "`MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES = 4096` | one snapshot's distinct (`action`, input-token) pairs as admitted"
findings.problem: [new in changed text] The row's subject ("one snapshot's … pairs") and its new modifier ("as admitted") are in different frames: the prose makes the enforced quantity "the distinct pairs a tree's fold has ever admitted", which can exceed a snapshot's surviving pairs. Direction is safe — the enforced check is the stricter one, so the `bindings/v1` pair-total bound still holds and no read cost changes — but amendment item 1 copies this table into `schemas/README.md`, shipping the ambiguity.
findings.fix: State the checked quantity in the row: "the distinct (`action`, input-token) pairs one tree's fold may admit, which bounds its snapshot's surviving pairs". No new constant, no change to the check.

findings.location: Goals, first list — "`GameContext` carries the lookup key, the digit appid, the install path, and the *owning* Steam root and library" (also Context's "lets a codec be told *which* Steam root and library own a discovered game")
findings.problem: regression: the revision replaced `root: PathBuf` with `roots: Vec<PathBuf> // every root the scan resolved, core byte order`, and the owning root now exists only on `ScanRecord`, never on the context. The one sentence stating what the context carries to a codec still describes the pre-revision struct, and it is the sentence an implementer starts from.
findings.fix: Rewrite the Goals bullet as "the lookup key, the digit appid, the install path, every resolved Steam root and the owning library" and drop "*which* … own" from the Context sentence. No struct change.

findings.location: §Read discipline and budgets, aggregate paragraph — "since §The first family caps a tree's reads at `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` the product also ceilings the *opens*, so the worst case is `17 × 32 × MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS` (544 MiB)"
findings.problem: new: the revised `detect` opens every path-grammar match "through `read::open_capped` and `read::decode` for that content test" and `extract` still "reads only located files, through `read.rs`", so each tree costs up to 2 × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES opens and twice the bytes — the ceiling on opens is 1,088 and the worst-case read ~1.06 GiB, not 544 MiB. Contract-tree amendment 1 requires this product to be stated in `schemas/README.md`, so the error ships in prose.
findings.fix: State the aggregate as `2 × (MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 1) × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` opens, or say `detect` hands `extract` the bytes it decoded — the latter replaces "extract reads only located files, through `read.rs`".

findings.location: §Read discipline — "`MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME` is the one silent bound — past the 16th tree a game's remaining local users are simply absent"
findings.problem: new: the same revision added two more bounds that truncate with no named refusal and no status ("a further match is skipped and counted the way an entry past `MAX_LOCATE_ENTRIES_PER_TREE` is"), and Test strategy 4 now files `017-B3`'s refusal away as "`017-B3`'s type invariant, behind the walk's skip-and-count", i.e. unreachable on the only path that counts files. The section documents one silent truncation where it has three, the ADR-named located-set budget no longer refuses in practice, contrary to the same section's "drift becomes loud rather than a silently shorter snapshot". The two new constants are also the run's only budgets with no recorded basis (`design-time` in the Source column, no surveyed entry count or document size), so nothing establishes that 16,384 entries covers a real prefix rather than quietly shortening it.
findings.fix: Mark in the table's `Bounds` column which bounds truncate silently and where their count surfaces (or make the 33rd match a named refusal), and add one clause per design-time constant naming the observed value it was sized from.

findings.location: §The CLI face, item 1 — "a concretely typed copy of that selection, since `scan_records()` and `roots()` are inherent methods and not on the trait"
findings.problem: new: the revision makes the duplication explicit. `apps/discovery-cli/src/main.rs:129-142` holds the selection (the `from_host()` pair when `--steam-root` is empty, the `cfg(not(windows))`/`cfg(windows)` `from_roots` branch otherwise) and `bindings.rs` now re-implements it — the second copy of root selection this document's own Options rejected option (b) was rejected for ("lets two trees of code disagree about which roots exist"), with `017-L5`'s pinned `list` the thing future drift hits.
findings.fix: One CLI-private helper returning the concretely typed plugin pair plus `roots()`, which `list` coerces into its existing `Vec<Box<dyn DiscoveryPlugin>>` (identical plugin order and rows, so the pinned suites are untouched) and both faces call — replacing the copy, adding nothing.

findings.location: §Determinism — "across documents, deduplicated by each document's `UserCandidates.tree_root` — tree identity, never rendered — the first stating it once", beside §`bindings/v1`'s "two trees may share a `user` label … so a consumer unions same-`user` documents' entries"

Two contract-shaping rules now live only in proposal prose.
findings.fix: Tag the dedup clause as the face's rendering rule (§The CLI face item 3 already invokes it) and add same-`user` non-uniqueness to the `spec.md` contents list. No shape change.

ambiguities: Options considered — "refusing the snapshot (the death of this run's purpose, which is first manifests)": the word order of "which is first manifests" is compressed; read as "the run's first purpose is manifests" and left unchanged.

Goals / Non-goals — "fixture trees for the two launcher contexts whose roots a record can justify": which two contexts (SteamUserdata and ProtonPrefix anchors) is only inferable from §Config-path resolvers; left unchanged.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/registry.rs:36-50
findings.problem: §The registry states that "an appid-table hit claims regardless of what the grammar's files turn out to contain — that is exactly 017-L2's family-confirmed-but-files-not-found case, and it is the visible one." claim_with instead treats the appid table as only selecting whose detect runs (registry.rs:37-39: "a table family whose own detect declines does not claim"), so an appid-listed family that locates nothing yields no claim and the face prints claim-refused (exit 3) — the collapse 017-L2 forbids ("never collapsed into an empty entry list or a non-claim"). Latent only in shipped configuration (A21: unreal-ini's appids() is empty); it bites when 017-R4 lands appid data and a listed game has never been launched. tests/registry.rs:169-178 asserts the rule but uses an appid (900998) that is not in AppidOwner::appids() (900100), so the declined-detect-through-the-table case is unpinned.
findings.fix: In pass 1, claim on the table hit itself: run detect to populate per_user but treat None as a claim with empty per_user carrying Evidence::AppidTable (bindings.rs:257-259 then reports family-confirmed-files-absent as designed); or keep the implemented rule and record it as a declared deviation in 03-build-notes.md plus a Revision-log line, and pin it with a table-listed family whose detect declines.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:99-104
findings.problem: extract re-sorts the per-user groups by tree_root byte order alone (as does apps/discovery-cli/src/bindings.rs:152-159), but the ordering law shipped in this diff — schemas/bindings/v1/spec.md:85-95, "documents and their user-tree groups in user_trees order", with "a conforming serializer emits … arrays in exactly the order above" — defines user_trees order as TreeKind declaration order then root byte order (paths.rs:1-12; proposal:317-319). For the ordinary mixed case (one root that is its own library, both a userdata/<steamid>/<appid> tree and a <lib>/steamapps/compatdata/<appid>/… tree) the two orders are opposite: "steamapps" sorts before "userdata", so the shipped serializer emits the Proton document first where the contract says the SteamUserdata one comes first. --json array order and table row order are affected; determinism is unaffected, and no test pins which order is the order (tests/determinism.rs:48-76 only proves arrival-order insensitivity).
findings.fix: Make the diff self-consistent: either carry TreeKind on UserCandidates and sort by (kind, tree_root) so the emitted order is user_trees order, or amend schemas/bindings/v1/spec.md §Ordering (plus a Revision-log line) to name tree-root byte order as the document order, since that spec is the third-party conformance text.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:143-168
findings.problem: game_key reconstructs the snapshot's `game` lookup key by scanning the located tree's path components for the first component named "compatdata" (next component must be digits) or "userdata" (must be exactly two components from the end), and returns None otherwise, which extract turns into ExtractionRefusal::UnreadableFile (unreal_ini.rs:108-111) and the face prints as extraction-refused, exit 5. A Steam root or library path that merely contains a component with either literal name (a root at /data/userdata, a library folder named compatdata) breaks the reconstruction for a game whose files are perfectly readable. The authoritative value was available at detect time as ctx.lookup_key, and `game` can only ever be steam/<ctx.appid> because both templates are built from it.
findings.fix: Have user_trees carry the lookup key (or the appid) from GameContext onto UserTree/UserCandidates, have detect copy it into UserCandidates, and have extract use it directly; delete the component-scan heuristic.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:184-245
findings.problem: The locate walk is breadth-first (VecDeque with push_back/pop_front; its own comment calls it a "Byte-ordered level walk"), while §The first family (proposal:498-499) specifies "walks each UserTree depth-first in byte order". Determinism and the depth, entry-count and MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES caps are unaffected; only which files a tree with more than MAX_LOCATE_ENTRIES_PER_TREE entries surfaces as its first 32 candidates can differ. This is an undeclared gap between proposal and code (checklist item 3); severity reflects its behaviour, not the declaration gap, which cannot be checked because 03-build-notes.md is outside this seat's inputs.
findings.fix: Record the level-order walk and its reason (the entry budget fails shallow-first, the friendlier degradation) in 03-build-notes.md, or change the walk to depth-first byte order as the proposal states.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:335-339
findings.problem: Fold::clear empties `seen` along with `pairs`, keeping only `admitted`, so a file that alternates a bare `!Bindings=` with the same `+Bindings=(Name=…,Command=…)` re-admits an identical pair each cycle and charges MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES again. The design counts "the distinct (action, input-token) pairs a tree's fold has ever admitted", so the counter can reach MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES + 1 on a fold holding one pair, producing a SnapshotEntryBudget refusal (exit 5) for a document that is in budget. Fails closed, and needs roughly 4097 clear-and-re-add cycles inside one ≤1 MiB file.
findings.fix: Clear only `pairs` in clear() and leave `seen` populated (or track every pair ever seen in a set and drive `admitted` from its cardinality), so "distinct pairs ever admitted" is literally the counter.

findings.location: apps/discovery-cli/src/bindings.rs:249-268
findings.problem: §The CLI face step 3 runs from_record → claim → extract per matching record and step 5 exits the highest-ranked status reported; this face merges every record's claim per family (MergedClaim::absorb, bindings.rs:118-148), extracts once, and asks whether any document has entries (bindings.rs:257-259). A run over two records of one slug — one whose located store states nothing readable, one whose store has bindings — therefore exits 0/ok where the per-record reading exits 4/family-confirmed-files-absent. The documents themselves are the same either way (tree-identity dedup makes merging equivalent to per-record extraction), so only the status is affected.
findings.fix: Derive family-confirmed-files-absent per record (a record whose own claim's documents all fold empty) before taking the max, or state in 03-build-notes.md that the status is computed per family over the merged claim.

findings.location: crates/codecs/Cargo.toml:16-20
findings.problem: §crates/codecs layout (proposal:214-217) lists serde_json as a dev-dependency; the crate declares it as a load dependency, because snapshot.rs's loader is a JSON parser and must have it at run time. The code is right and the proposal's line is internally inconsistent; the lockfile cost is zero (serde_json already resolved, A12). It remains an undeclared gap against the proposal's dependency list.
findings.fix: Add one line to 03-build-notes.md recording that serde_json is a load dependency of bindforge-codecs, so the deviation is on the record.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:194-243 (esp. 197, 217, 240-242)
findings.problem: The locate walk rebuilds every child path from `entry.file_name().to_string_lossy()` (`dir.join(&name)`) instead of `entry.path()`. For an entry whose name is not valid UTF-8 — legal on ext4 and ordinary on the exFAT/NTFS libraries the Compatibility matrix lists as supported — the joined path names something that never existed: a grammar-shaped file falls into the `Err(_)` arm written for "a match the reader refuses is located on path grammar alone", so an invented path is recorded as a located candidate and `extract` later refuses the whole game as `UnreadableFile` (face exit 5, `extraction-refused`); a non-UTF-8 directory is queued as a nonexistent path, so its whole subtree is silently skipped with no skip-count to account for it. §The first family's "extract reads only located files" and the matrix's supported-layout posture are both unmet; no fixture exercises it because every fixture name is ASCII.
findings.fix: Keep `entry.path()` for the queue and for `candidates.push`, use `entry.file_name()` (OsStr bytes) as the sort key, and split the `Err` arm: locate-on-path-grammar only for `FileOverBudget`/`UndecodableText`, skip-and-count for `UnreadableFile`.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:506-511 (with crates/codecs/src/snapshot.rs:305-308)
findings.problem: `tree_relative` emits `strip_prefix(..).to_string_lossy()`, i.e. platform-native separators, into the contract's `provenance.files`. On the Windows host the face runs on (matrix row: "the root-relative trees resolve and are stat'd", and `<root>/userdata/<steamid>/<appid>` is the Windows Steam layout), the same layout states `Saved\Config\WindowsNoEditor\Engine.ini` instead of the `/`-spelled document the spec and fixtures state, and the byte-order sort of `files` changes (`\`=0x5C vs `/`=0x2F) — breaking the field's own stated portability rule (§`bindings/v1`: "the same layout states the same document on any machine"). The read side already assumes `/` (`.max(file.matches('/').count() + 1)`), so the normalization exists on one half only.
findings.fix: Build the contract spelling once with `components().map(|c| c.as_os_str().to_string_lossy()).join("/")` and use it for the document, the sort and refusal messages; keep absolute native paths only in `--probe` output, and pin the `/`-spelling in a loader/honesty assertion.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/paths.rs:127-136 (comment at 133-135)
findings.problem: The comment promises "A17's broken-prefix case degrades to files-absent", and the Compatibility matrix's NTFS/exFAT row promises `family-confirmed-files-absent` (exit 4). Shipped behavior differs: a link-anchored prefix yields no tree, `unreal_ini::detect` returns `None` when nothing is located (unreal_ini.rs:73-90), and `appids()` is empty (unreal_ini.rs:67-71), so no `appid-table` claim exists to produce status 4 — the game answers `claim-refused` (exit 3). The safety half of the row (no hang, no out-of-tree read) does hold.
findings.fix: State the degradation truthfully: correct the comment and the matrix row (via the §Rollout 8 ledger hand-off) to `claim-refused`/exit 3 with §The registry's reason, or give the row a real route to exit 4.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:251-258
findings.problem: `grammar_match` compares `Saved`, `Config` and the `.ini` suffix byte-exactly, an unstated case-sensitivity assumption on the case-insensitive filesystems the face can run on (Windows row). Neither the doc comment, `schemas/bindings/v1/spec.md`, nor §The first family records that the grammar is case-exact, so a `saved/config` or `X.INI` tree is silently out of grammar.
findings.fix: One sentence in the `grammar_match` doc comment (and in spec.md, since it is a locate-time contract fact) naming the match as case-exact by design — or match the extension case-insensitively and say so.

findings.location: crates/codecs/tests/paths.rs:140-181 and crates/codecs/tests/unreal_ini.rs:183-224
findings.problem: §The first family names a `symlinked-prefix` fixture tree with a `#[cfg(not(unix))]` early return; no such tree ships (fixture set: steam-userdata, proton-prefix, bom-utf16, defaults-only, bindings-absent, broken-tuple) — link coverage moved to temp-dir links, and only the `paths.rs` test has the compile-only `cfg(not(unix))` arm; the `unreal_ini.rs` link test has none. Linux coverage is equivalent (verified: `cargo test -p bindforge-codecs --locked` → 64 tests, symlink tests execute), so this is plan drift rather than a gap.
findings.fix: Record the shipped shape in `03-build-notes.md` (links created at test time, no committed `symlinked-prefix` tree) and add the matching `#[cfg(not(unix))]` arm to the `unreal_ini` link test.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/snapshot.rs:296-319
findings.problem: The bindings/v1 loader — the boundary validator for a shareable, untrusted document — checks provenance.files only for empty and POSIX-absolute spellings (`file.is_empty() || file.starts_with('/')`). `"../../../../etc/passwd"`, `"Saved/Config/../../../etc/crontab"`, `"C:/Windows/win.ini"`, `"..\\..\\x"` and `"./x.ini"` all load: `Path::components()` counts a `ParentDir` as an ordinary component and stays inside MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH (8), and the Windows drive/UNC and backslash forms pass on every platform. Nothing in crates/codecs checks ParentDir/traversal/is_absolute, and the invalid-fixture corpus has only the depth case (files-depth-files.json), so the green gate cannot establish the property. This run's own amendment at schemas/manifests/v1/spec.md:128-136 makes those strings executable data — the fingerprint is 'the located config files' octets concatenated in the extracted snapshot's sorted provenance.files order' — so ADR-017's named consumers (manifest authoring, the 017-R1 apply face, the UI import) must resolve entries that a doctored document can point outside the tree it claims to have read, and 017-L3's provenance claim stops being checkable by any consumer that trusts the loader.
findings.fix: Refuse any files entry that is not a plain '/'-separated sequence of `Component::Normal`: reject Prefix/RootDir/CurDir/ParentDir (naming `files`, as the other refusals do) and reject raw spellings containing `\\` or `:` so the Windows resolver cannot be fed an alternate absolute form. State it in schemas/bindings/v1/spec.md's Bounds bullet and add schemas/bindings/v1/fixtures/invalid/files-traversal__files.json so every_invalid_schema_fixture_is_refused_naming_its_key pins the refusal name. The family's tree_relative output already emits only Normal components, so no valid fixture or produced document changes.

findings.location: apps/discovery-cli/src/bindings.rs:293
findings.problem: The `extraction-refused` line prints `format!("{error}")` raw, and ExtractionRefusal's Display (crates/codecs/src/codec.rs:158-191) interpolates path fields that come from filesystem names — `tree_relative`'s `to_string_lossy` over `read_dir` entries (crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:506-511) and `tree_root.display()` (unreal_ini.rs:109-111). Linux file names may contain ESC and other control bytes, so a game's own config tree — the input class this design calls untrusted — can emit raw escape sequences (cursor movement, OSC title/clipboard, color resets) onto the operator's stderr. Stdout is already safe via cell() (apps/discovery-cli/src/main.rs:348-356) and serde_json escaping, so only the error line breaks the discipline the run states for its own messages (schemas/bindings/v1/spec.md:104-106: every message single-line, control-free, truncating, echoed values through escape_and_truncate) — which the loader refusals honor (snapshot.rs:95-105, pinned by tests/snapshot.rs:89-109) and UnparsableEntry's detail honors via short(), but the paths do not.
findings.fix: Escape at the sink — `eprintln!("error: {}", bindforge_core::escape_and_truncate(&message))` at bindings.rs:293 (and in `refused` for the scan-failure line) — or render every `path` field through escape_and_truncate inside ExtractionRefusal's Display. Pin it with one fixture route whose located directory name carries a control byte, asserting the `error:` line is single-line and control-free.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:226-243
findings.problem: The locate walk's per-tree open cap gates on `candidates.files.len()` — the LOCATED set — not on the number of files opened. A path-grammar match that decodes cleanly but lacks `[/Script/Engine.PlayerInput]` is opened via `read::open_capped`, buffered whole, decoded and scanned, and never advances the counter that gates the next open, so opens per tree are bounded only by `MAX_LOCATE_ENTRIES_PER_TREE` (16,384) rather than `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` (32). This contradicts the aggregate budget this same diff ships in `schemas/README.md:202-208` ("the product caps the *opens* too — so the worst case is ... (544 MiB) read per game") and `schemas/bindings/v1/spec.md:74-78`, and the proposal's §The first family ("At most `MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES` path-grammar matches per tree ... are opened through `read::open_capped` and `read::decode` for that content test"). Practical worst case: every `…/Saved/Config/<dir>/*.ini` under each walked tree is opened and buffered at up to 1 MiB each — reachable without an adversary, since a Proton prefix tree reaches the grammar at 7 relative components (`AppData/Local/<Game>/Saved/Config/<platform>/<name>.ini`, within `MAX_LOCATE_DEPTH` = 8), so one query reads every game's config in that prefix. The design's accepted 544 MiB/game risk therefore does not bound what shipped, and no test can see it: `tests/unreal_ini.rs:262-280` uses 33 matches that all state the section, the one input where "matches located" and "files opened" coincide.
findings.fix: Count opens independently of locating: add `let mut opened = 0usize;` beside `examined`, test `if opened >= MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES { continue; }` before `read::open_capped`, and increment it for every grammar match the walk attempts to test, so the skip-and-count matches the README's "caps the opens too". Add the missing pin: N grammar-matching `.ini` files that do NOT state the section plus one that does, sorted past the cap, asserting the stating file is not located.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:232 and crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:117-121,516-533
findings.problem: `Detection` carries paths rather than contents, so `extract` re-reads and re-decodes each located file that `detect` already opened, buffered and scanned for the content test. Even with the open cap fixed, one `discovery bindings <slug>` run reads 2× the `(MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 1) × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES × MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS` = 544 MiB per game that `schemas/README.md:202-208` states as the worst case, because the aggregate sentence counts only one pass.
findings.fix: Either carry the already-decoded text on `UserCandidates` (or a private per-`detect` read cache keyed by path) so `extract` folds what `detect` read, keeping `read_and_decode` only for the located-on-path-grammar-only case; or state the doubled pass in `schemas/README.md` and `schemas/bindings/v1/spec.md` as `2 × (MAX_USER_DIRS_PER_GAME + 1) × MAX_CANDIDATE_FILES × MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS`, noting `--probe` pays one pass and the extracting face two.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:329-333
findings.problem: `Fold::remove` allocates a two-String key and then unconditionally `retain`s over the whole working set (up to `MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES + 1` = 4,097 pairs) for every `-Bindings=`/`!Bindings=` line — including removals of pairs the set never held, which consume no `admitted` budget and are therefore bounded only by `MAX_BINDING_FILE_OCTETS`. A 1 MiB file of ~40-byte removal tuples is ~25k lines, each scanning ~4k pairs ≈ 10^8 predicate evaluations, and `extract` folds up to 32 located files per tree across up to 17 trees: O(removal lines × working set), where the named budgets were meant to be the only bound on untrusted config input.
findings.fix: `seen` and `pairs` are maintained in lockstep by `add`/`remove`/`clear`, so membership is exact: build the key once, `if !self.seen.contains(&key) { return; }` before touching `pairs`, and reuse the one key for the set removal and the retain predicate. Better, keep the working set in a `BTreeSet<(action, input)>` so removal is O(log n) at no cost — `entries()` (unreal_ini.rs:343-358) already sorts by action then input byte order.

findings.location: crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:194-206
findings.problem: The walk collects `read_dir`'s entire output into `Vec<(String, DirEntry)>` and sorts it before the loop applies the `examined >= MAX_LOCATE_ENTRIES_PER_TREE` gate, so transient allocation and the O(m log m) sort are bounded by the largest directory under the tree root, not by the budget `lib.rs:53-55` presents as bounding the walk ("entries the locate walk examines below one `UserTree` root"). The `ProtonPrefix` anchor (`paths.rs:117-137`) is a home-directory tree, precisely where large entry-count directories live.
findings.fix: Test the budget at the top of the queue loop before `read_dir` (an over-budget walk should not enter another directory) and cap the listing to the remaining budget (`entries.take(room)`) — determinism is unaffected, since which entries a truncated walk examines is already unspecified beyond the stop-and-count law pinned at `tests/unreal_ini.rs:231-256`. findings.location: crates/codecs/src/snapshot.rs:311-315 vs crates/codecs/src/families/unreal_ini.rs:280-287, :128-134
